translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai once told Zheng gently, "Your distant ancestor showed loyalty by leaving the court; you show loyalty by coming to it — truly accumulated virtue brings later reward, and your house adds honor with each generation."

sentences.zh: 」整遠祖漢建威將軍邁，不為王莽屈，其子稱避地河右。

translations.literal: Zheng's distant ancestor was Mai, Han General Who Establishes Might, who would not submit to Wang Mang; his son Cheng took refuge west of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's distant ancestor was Mai, Han General Who Establishes Might, who refused to bow to Wang Mang; his son Cheng took refuge in the Hexi region.

sentences.zh: 故太祖稱之云。

translations.literal: Hence the Grand Progenitor spoke of him thus.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said what he did.

sentences.zh: 尋除驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening-office Equal in Three Departments, with the added post of palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Grand General of Fast Cavalry and opening-office equal in three departments, with the added title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 太祖又謂整曰：「卿勳同婁、項，義等骨肉，立身敦雅，可以範人。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor again said to Zheng: "Your merit equals Lou and Xiang; your righteousness is like kin; your conduct is upright and refined and can serve as a model for others."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai again told Zheng, "Your merit matches that of Lou and Xiang, your loyalty is like family, and your upright, refined conduct can guide others."

sentences.zh: 」遂賜姓宇文氏，並賜名整焉。

translations.literal: He thereupon granted him the surname Yuwen and also gave him the name Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore granted him the surname Yuwen and the given name Zheng.

sentences.zh: 宗人二百餘戶，竝列屬籍。

translations.literal: More than two hundred households of his clan were all entered on the register of affiliation.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred households of his clan were enrolled in the Yuwen affiliation register.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，拜司憲中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was appointed Central Grand Master of Law Enforcement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was made central grand master of law enforcement.

sentences.zh: 處法平允，為當時所稱。

translations.literal: In applying the law he was fair and even, and was praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: He applied the law evenhandedly and won praise at the time.

sentences.zh: 進爵彭陽縣公，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced in nobility to Duke of Pengyang county and given one thousand added fief households.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Duke of Pengyang with one thousand added fief households.

sentences.zh: 初，梁興州刺史席固以州來附，太祖以固為豐州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liang Inspector of Xing Province Xi Gu had submitted the prefecture; the Grand Progenitor made Gu inspector of Feng Province.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liang's inspector of Xing Province, Xi Gu, had submitted his prefecture, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai made him inspector of Feng Province.

sentences.zh: 固莅職旣久，猶習梁法，凡所施為，多虧治典。

translations.literal: Gu had held office a long time and still followed Liang law; in whatever he did he often fell short of the governing code.
translations.idiomatic: Gu had governed for years and still followed Liang practices; much of what he did fell short of proper administration.

sentences.zh: 朝議密欲代之，而難其選。

translations.literal: Court opinion secretly wished to replace him, but found the choice difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The court quietly wanted to replace him but could not settle on the right man.

sentences.zh: 遂令整權鎮豐州，委以代固之略。

translations.literal: Zheng was therefore ordered to hold Feng Province in temporary command and was entrusted with the plan to replace Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was therefore sent to hold Feng Province temporarily and given charge of replacing Gu.

sentences.zh: 整廣布威恩，傾身撫接，數月之間，化洽州府。

translations.literal: Zheng broadly spread authority and kindness, devoting himself to winning men; within several months the prefecture and headquarters were transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng combined firm authority with kindness and worked tirelessly among the people; within months the whole prefecture was transformed.

sentences.zh: 於是除整豐州刺史，以固為湖州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zheng was appointed Inspector of Feng Province, and Gu was made inspector of Hu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was then made inspector of Feng Province, and Gu was transferred to Hu Province.

sentences.zh: 豐州舊治，不居人民，賦役參集，勞逸不均。

translations.literal: Feng Province's old seat did not lie among the people; taxes and corvée were gathered from many places, and toil and rest were unevenly distributed.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Province's old capital stood apart from the population; taxes and labor were drawn from scattered districts, and burdens fell unevenly.

sentences.zh: 整請移治武當，詔可其奏。

translations.literal: Zheng requested that the seat be moved to Wudang; an edict approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng asked to move the capital to Wudang, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 獎勵撫導，遷者如歸，旬月之間，城府周備。

translations.literal: He rewarded, encouraged, and guided the people; those who moved returned as if to their old home, and within a month the city walls and offices were complete.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded and guided the settlers; people came as though returning home, and within a month the city and offices were fully built.

sentences.zh: 固之遷也，其部曲多願留為整左右，整諭以朝制，弗之許也，流涕而去。

translations.literal: When Gu was transferred, many of his retainers wished to stay and serve at Zheng's side; Zheng explained the court's regulations and would not permit it, and they left in tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu departed, many of his retainers wanted to stay with Zheng; Zheng cited court rules and refused them, and they left in tears.

sentences.zh: 及整秩滿代至，民吏戀之，老幼送整，遠近畢集，數日停留，方得出界。

translations.literal: When Zheng's term ended and his replacement arrived, officials and people clung to him; old and young escorted Zheng; people gathered from near and far; for several days they delayed his departure before he could leave the border.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and his successor arrived, officials and commoners alike clung to him; old and young escorted him for days before he could cross the border.

sentences.zh: 其得人心如此。

translations.literal: Such was the way he won men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: That was how deeply he won people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 拜御正中大夫，出為中華郡守，轉同州司會，遷始州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Central Grand Master of Imperial Rectification, sent out as Administrator of Zhonghua commandery, transferred to provincial accountant of Tong Province, and promoted to Inspector of Shi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made central grand master of imperial rectification, then administrator of Zhonghua commandery, provincial accountant of Tong Province, and finally inspector of Shi Province.

sentences.zh: 整雅識情偽，尤明政術，恭謹廉慎，常懼盈滿，故曆居內外，所在見稱。

translations.literal: Zheng finely understood human truth and falsehood and was especially clear in the arts of government; he was respectful, cautious, and incorrupt, and constantly feared excess — hence whether in central or local office, he was praised wherever he served.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng read men and affairs shrewdly and knew government well; respectful, careful, and incorrupt, he always feared overreach — and was praised in every post he held.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，進位大將軍，增邑通前二千一百戶。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe he was promoted to Great General, with fief households increased to two thousand one hundred in all with earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 6 he was promoted to great general, with his fief brought to two thousand one hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 晉公護之初執政也，欲委整以腹心。

translations.literal: When Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu first took power, he wished to entrust Zheng as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu first seized power, he wanted Zheng as a trusted inner counselor.

sentences.zh: 整辭不敢當，頗迕其意，護以此疎之。

translations.literal: Zheng declined, saying he dared not accept; he greatly went against Hu's wish, and for this Hu kept him at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng declined, saying he was unworthy; the refusal offended Hu, and Hu kept his distance thereafter.

sentences.zh: 及護誅，附會者咸伏法，而整獨保全。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, those who had attached themselves to him were all punished by law, while Zheng alone was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu was killed, his partisans were all punished, but Zheng alone escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 時人稱其先覺。

translations.literal: People of the time praised his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised his foresight.

sentences.zh: 建德二年卒，時年六十一。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Jiande, aged sixty-one at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiande year 2 at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加鄜宜豳鹽四州諸軍事、鄜州刺史，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted his former office, with the added posts of military affairs for Fu, Yi, Bin, and Yan four provinces and Inspector of Fu Province; his posthumous title was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former rank, with added command over military affairs in Fu, Yi, Bin, and Yan and the post of inspector of Fu; his posthumous title was Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子熙嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 熙字長熙。

translations.literal: Xi, styled Changxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, courtesy name Changxi.

sentences.zh: 性方雅，有度量，雖在私室，容止儼然。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and refined, with breadth of mind; even in private quarters his bearing remained dignified.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and dignified by nature, with a generous mind; even in private his bearing stayed composed.

sentences.zh: 非一時賢俊，未嘗與之遊處。

translations.literal: Unless they were outstanding men of the age, he never kept company with them.
translations.idiomatic: He kept company only with the finest men of the day.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，解音律，涉羣書，尤明《三禮》。

translations.literal: He was skilled at mounted archery, understood musical pitch, and read widely in the classics; he was especially versed in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in mounted archery and music, read widely, and was especially learned in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 累遷居職任，竝有能名。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions in office he held responsible posts, and in all had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted through successive offices, he earned a name for competence wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 大象中，位至吏部中大夫、儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: During the Daxiang era he reached Middle Grand Master in the Ministry of Personnel and Grand General with Equal Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daxiang era he rose to middle grand master in the Ministry of Personnel and grand general with equal protocol.

sentences.zh: 整弟休，幼聰敏，有文武材。

translations.literal: Zheng's younger brother Xiu was intelligent and keen from youth and possessed both civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's younger brother Xiu was bright from childhood and gifted in both civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 起家太學生。

translations.literal: He began his career as a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a student of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 後與整同起兵逐張保，授都督。

translations.literal: Later he joined Zheng in raising troops to drive out Zhang Bao and was appointed area commander.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Zheng in raising troops against Zhang Bao and was made area commander.

sentences.zh: 累遷大都督、樂安郡守。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he reached Grand Area Commander and Administrator of Le'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to grand area commander and administrator of Le'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 入為中外府樂曹參軍。

translations.literal: He entered office as music bureau adjutant of the Central and External Office.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as music bureau adjutant of the central and external office.

sentences.zh: 時諸功臣多為本州刺史，晉公護謂整曰：「以公勳望，應得本州，但朝廷藉公委任，無容遠出。

translations.literal: At the time many meritorious ministers served as inspectors of their home provinces; Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu said to Zheng: "By your merit and standing you ought to receive your home province, but the court relies on you for weighty duties and cannot allow you to go far away.
translations.idiomatic: Many great ministers then served as inspectors of their home provinces; Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu told Zheng, "By merit and standing you deserve your home province, but the court depends on you and cannot send you far away.

sentences.zh: 然公門之內，須有衣錦之榮。

translations.literal: Yet within your household there must be the honor of returning home in brocade."
translations.idiomatic: Still, your family ought to have the glory of a son returning in brocade."

sentences.zh: 」乃以休為燉煌郡守。

translations.literal: Xiu was therefore made Administrator of Dunhuang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was therefore made administrator of Dunhuang commandery.

sentences.zh: 在郡十餘年，甚有政績。

translations.literal: He governed the commandery for more than ten years with considerable administrative achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Dunhuang for more than ten years with marked success.

sentences.zh: 進位儀同三司，遷合州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to equal in three departments and transferred to Inspector of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was promoted to equal in three departments and transferred to inspector of He Province.

sentences.zh: 尋卒官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office.

sentences.zh: 司馬裔字遵胤，河內溫人也，晉宣帝弟太常馗之後。

translations.literal: Sima Yi, styled Zunyin, was a native of Wen in Henei, a descendant of Grand Commandant Kui, younger brother of Jin's Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi, courtesy name Zunyin, came from Wen in Henei. He was descended from Grand Commandant Kui, younger brother of Jin's Founding Emperor.

sentences.zh: 曾祖楚之，屬宋武帝誅晉氏戚屬，避難歸魏。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chuzhi, when Emperor Wu of Song executed the Jin imperial clansmen, fled in refuge to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chuzhi, when Emperor Wu of Song purged the Jin imperial kin, took refuge in Wei.

sentences.zh: 位至使持節、侍中、鎮西大將軍、開府儀同三司、朔州刺史，封琅邪王。

translations.literal: He reached the ranks of bearer of the staff, palace attendant, grand general who pacifies the west, opening-office equal in three departments, and inspector of Shuo Province, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi rose to bearer of the staff, palace attendant, grand general who pacifies the west, opening-office equal in three departments, and inspector of Shuo Province, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 裔少孤，有志操，州郡辟召，竝不應命。

translations.literal: Yi lost his father young; he had ambition and integrity; when the province and commandery summoned him, he accepted none of their offers.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was orphaned young and had strong character; when province and commandery tried to recruit him, he refused them all.

sentences.zh: 起家司徒府參軍事。

translations.literal: He began his career as staff officer in the Minister of Education's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as staff officer in the minister of education's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功，授中堅將軍、員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later, for military merit, he was given the ranks of steadfast general and supernumerary attendant cavalier at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for military merit, he was made steadfast general and supernumerary attendant cavalier at leisure.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，裔時在鄴，潛歸鄉里，志在立功。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Yi was then at Ye; he secretly returned to his home district, intent on achieving merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei withdrew westward, Yi was at Ye; he slipped back to his home district, determined to win distinction.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，大軍復弘農，乃於溫城起義，遣使送款。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, when the main army recovered Hongnong, he raised the standard at Wencheng and sent envoys to submit allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 3, when the main army recovered Hongnong, Yi raised the standard at Wencheng and sent envoys to declare allegiance.

sentences.zh: 與東魏將高永洛、王陵等晝夜交戰。

translations.literal: He fought day and night with Eastern Wei generals Gao Yongluo, Wang Ling, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He fought day and night against Eastern Wei generals Gao Yongluo, Wang Ling, and others.

sentences.zh: 衆寡不敵，義徒死傷過半。

translations.literal: Outnumbered, more than half his rebels were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, more than half his followers were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 及大軍東征，裔率所部從戰河橋，又別攻懷縣，獲其將吳輔叔。

translations.literal: When the main army marched east, Yi led his command in battle at He Bridge, and separately attacked Huai county, capturing their general Wu Fushu.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army marched east, Yi led his troops at He Bridge and separately stormed Huai county, capturing the enemy general Wu Fushu.

sentences.zh: 自此頻與東魏交戰，每有克獲。

translations.literal: From then on he frequently fought Eastern Wei and repeatedly had captures.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he fought Eastern Wei again and again and repeatedly took spoils.

sentences.zh: 六年，授河內郡守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Administrator of Henei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was made administrator of Henei commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋加持節、平東將軍、北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was given bearer of the staff, general who pacifies the east, and inspector of Northern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received bearer of the staff, general who pacifies the east, and inspector of Northern Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 八年，率其義衆入朝。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he led his rebel followers to court.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he led his rebel followers to court.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，特蒙賞勞。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor commended this and he received special rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai commended this and gave him special rewards.

sentences.zh: 頃之，河內有四千餘家歸附，竝裔之鄉舊，乃授前將軍、太中大夫，領河內郡守，令安集流民。

translations.literal: Before long more than four thousand households in Henei submitted—all were Yi's old neighbors from home; he was thereupon given the ranks of vanguard general and grand master of palace grandee, ordered to hold the prefecture of Henei and settle the displaced.
translations.idiomatic: Before long more than four thousand households in Henei submitted, all of them Yi's old neighbors; he was thereupon made vanguard general and grand master of palace grandee, put in charge of Henei, and ordered to settle the displaced.

sentences.zh: 十三年，攻拔東魏平齊、柳泉、蓼塢三城，獲其鎮將李熙之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he stormed and took the three Eastern Wei cities of Pingqi, Liuquan, and Liaowu, capturing their garrison commander Li Xizhi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he stormed the three Eastern Wei cities of Pingqi, Liuquan, and Liaowu and captured their garrison commander Li Xizhi.

sentences.zh: 加授都督。

translations.literal: He was additionally given the rank of area commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made area commander.

sentences.zh: 十五年，太祖令山東立義諸將等能率衆入關者，竝加重賞。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Grand Progenitor ordered that all generals east of the mountains who had raised the standard and could lead their followers through the passes into Guanzhong would receive enhanced rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered that every general east of the mountains who had risen in loyalty and could lead followers through the passes into Guanzhong would receive enhanced rewards.

sentences.zh: 裔領戶千室先至，太祖欲以封裔。

translations.literal: Yi arrived first leading a thousand households; the Grand Progenitor wished to enfeoff Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi arrived first at the head of a thousand households, and Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai wished to enfeoff him.

sentences.zh: 裔固辭曰：「立義之士，辭鄉里，捐親戚，遠歸皇化者，皆是誠心內發，豈裔能率之乎。

translations.literal: Yi firmly declined, saying: "The men who rose in loyalty, left their home districts, abandoned kin, and came from afar to submit to imperial civilization—all did so from sincere hearts within. How could Yi have led them?
translations.idiomatic: Yi firmly declined, saying, "The men who rose in loyalty left their homes, abandoned kin, and came from afar to submit to the throne—all from sincere hearts within. How could I have led them?

sentences.zh: 今以封 裔，便是賣義士以求榮，非所願也。

translations.literal: Now to enfeoff Yi would be to sell loyal men for personal glory; that is not what I wish."
translations.idiomatic: To enfeoff me now would be to trade on loyal men for my own glory, and that is not what I wish."

sentences.zh: 」太祖善而從之。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor approved and followed his wish.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai approved and accepted his refusal.

sentences.zh: 授帥都督，拜其妻元為襄城郡公主。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief area commander, and his wife Yuan was enfeoffed as Princess of Xiangcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief area commander, and his wife Yuan was enfeoffed as Princess of Xiangcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 十六年，大軍東伐，裔請為前鋒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, when the main army marched east to attack, Yi asked to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16, when the main army marched east, Yi asked to serve as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 遂入建州，破東魏將劉雅興，拔其五城。

translations.literal: He thereupon entered Jian Province, defeated Eastern Wei general Liu Yaxing, and stormed five cities.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Jian Province, defeated Eastern Wei general Liu Yaxing, and took five cities.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，除巴州刺史，進使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵琅邪縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was appointed Inspector of Ba Province, promoted to bearer of the staff, grand general of agile cavalry, and opening-office equal in three departments, advanced to Baron of Langye county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Yi was made inspector of Ba Province, promoted to bearer of the staff, grand general of agile cavalry, and opening-office equal in three departments, and raised to baron of Langye with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，入為御伯中大夫，增邑通前一千五百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding he entered office as middle grand master in the Office of Imperial Bearer, with fief households increased to one thousand five hundred in all with earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 2 he entered the capital as middle grand master in the Office of Imperial Bearer, with his fief brought to one thousand five hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 四年，轉御正中大夫，進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to middle grand master of imperial rectification and advanced in enfeoffment to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was transferred to middle grand master of imperial rectification and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 大軍東討，裔率義兵與少師楊摽守軹關，卽授懷州刺史、東道慰勞大使。

translations.literal: When the main army marched east to punish the enemy, Yi led rebel troops together with Junior Preceptor Yang Biao to hold Zhiguan Pass; he was thereupon appointed Inspector of Huai Province and eastern-route reward-and-comfort commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army marched east, Yi led rebel troops with Junior Preceptor Yang Biao to hold Zhiguan Pass and was thereupon made inspector of Huai Province and eastern-route reward-and-comfort commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉始州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Inspector of Shi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was transferred to inspector of Shi Province.

sentences.zh: 天和初，信州蠻酋冉令賢等反，連結二千餘里。

translations.literal: At the opening of Tianhe, Man chieftains Ran Lingxian and others rebelled, linking territory for more than two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianhe, Man chieftains such as Ran Lingxian rebelled across more than two thousand li of territory.

sentences.zh: 裔隨上庸公陸騰討之。

translations.literal: Yi followed Duke of Shangyong Lu Teng in attacking them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi followed Duke of Shangyong Lu Teng against them.

sentences.zh: 裔自開州道入，先遣使宣示禍福。

translations.literal: Yi entered by the Kaizhou route and first sent envoys to set forth fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yi entered by the Kaizhou route and first sent envoys to explain the consequences of submission and resistance.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋冉三公等三十餘城皆來降附。

translations.literal: Man chieftains Ran Sanggong and others in more than thirty cities all came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Man chieftains such as Ran Sanggong in more than thirty cities all submitted.

sentences.zh: 進次雙城，蠻酋向寶勝等率其種落，據險自固。

translations.literal: Advancing to Shuangcheng, Man chieftain Xiang Baosheng led his tribes to hold the defiles and fortify themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Shuangcheng, Man chieftain Xiang Baosheng led his tribes to hold the defiles and dig in.

sentences.zh: 向天王之徒，為其外援。

translations.literal: Xiang Tianwang and his followers served as their external support.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Tianwang and his followers served as their outside support.

sentences.zh: 裔晝夜攻圍，腹背受敵。

translations.literal: Yi attacked and besieged day and night, attacked from front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Yi besieged them day and night and was himself attacked from front and rear.

sentences.zh: 自春至秋，五十餘戰。

translations.literal: From spring to autumn there were more than fifty battles.
translations.idiomatic: From spring to autumn there were more than fifty engagements.

sentences.zh: 寶勝糧仗俱竭，力屈乃降。

translations.literal: Baosheng's grain and weapons were both exhausted; his strength failed and he then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Baosheng's grain and arms were exhausted and his strength failed, he submitted.

sentences.zh: 時尚有籠東一城未下，尋亦拔之。

translations.literal: At the time Longdong city alone had not yet fallen; soon it too was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Only Longdong city still held out; before long it too was taken.

sentences.zh: 又獲賊帥冉西梨、向天王等。

translations.literal: They also captured rebel leaders Ran Xili and Xiang Tianwang.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Xili, Xiang Tianwang, and other rebel chiefs were also taken captive.

sentences.zh: 出師再期，羣蠻率服。

translations.literal: Two seasons on campaign, and the Man tribes all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Within two seasons on campaign, the Man tribes all submitted.

sentences.zh: 拜信州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Inspector of Xin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made inspector of Xin Province.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷潼州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Inspector of Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was transferred to inspector of Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 六年，徵拜大將軍，除西寧州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned and appointed Great General and made Inspector of Xining Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was recalled, made great general, and appointed inspector of Xining Province.

sentences.zh: 未及之部，卒于京師。

translations.literal: Before he reached his post he died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the capital before he could take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 裔性清約，不事生業，所得俸祿，竝散之親戚，身死之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Yi by nature was frugal and restrained; he did not pursue livelihood; the salary he received he distributed entirely to kin; on the day he died his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was frugal by nature and did not pursue wealth; he gave all his salary to kin, and when he died his household had nothing left.

sentences.zh: 宅宇卑陋，喪庭無所，有詔為起祠堂焉。

translations.literal: His dwelling was low and mean; there was no place for the mourning hall; an edict ordered that a memorial hall be built for him.
translations.idiomatic: His house was humble and there was no room for mourning rites; an edict ordered a memorial hall built for him.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍，加懷邵汾晉四州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Great General, plus Governor of the four provinces Huai, Shao, Fen, and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made great general and governor of Huai, Shao, Fen, and Jin provinces.

sentences.zh: 諡曰定。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Ding.

sentences.zh: 子偘嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 偘字道遷，少敢勇，未弱冠，便從戎旅。

translations.literal: Kan, styled Daobian, from youth was bold and brave; before he had reached the capping age he already joined the army.
translations.idiomatic: Kan, courtesy name Daobian, was bold from youth; before he came of age he was already in the army.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，隨少師楊摽東征。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding he followed Junior Preceptor Yang Biao on the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 4 he followed Junior Preceptor Yang Biao on the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 與齊人交戰，摽為敵所擒，偘力戰得免。

translations.literal: Fighting with Qi troops, Biao was captured by the enemy; Kan fought fiercely and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: In fighting with Qi troops, Biao was taken by the enemy; Kan fought hard and escaped.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，授右侍上士，加都督，進大都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe he was appointed right attendant gentleman, given the added rank of area commander, and promoted to grand area commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 2 he was made right attendant gentleman, given the added rank of area commander, and promoted to grand area commander.

sentences.zh: 從大軍攻晉州，以功授使持節、車騎將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Following the main army in attacking Jin Province, for merit he was given bearer of the staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and equal in three departments.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the main army against Jin Province and, for merit, was made bearer of the staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and equal in three departments.

sentences.zh: 又從平並、鄴，除樂安郡守。

translations.literal: He again followed in pacifying Bing and Ye and was appointed Administrator of Le'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He again took part in pacifying Bing and Ye and was made administrator of Le'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 後更論晉州及平齊勳，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Later, when Jin Province and the Pingqi merit were reviewed again, he was given the added ranks of grand general of agile cavalry and opening-office equal in three departments.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when merit at Jin Province and in the Pingqi campaign was reviewed again, he received the added ranks of grand general of agile cavalry and opening-office equal in three departments.

sentences.zh: 遷兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 未之部而卒。

translations.literal: Before he reached his post he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before he could report to his new command.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加豫州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted his former office, plus Inspector of Yu Province; posthumous title Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously confirmed in his former rank and made inspector of Yu Province; his posthumous title was Hui.

sentences.zh: 子運嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 裴果字戎昭，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Guo, styled Rongzhao, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Guo, courtesy name Rongzhao, came from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖思賢，魏青州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sixian was Inspector of Qing Province in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sixian had been Wei inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 父遵，齊州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zun was Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zun was inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 果少慷慨，有志略。

translations.literal: Guo from youth was generous and resolute and had ambition and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Guo was generous and resolute, with real ambition and strategic sense.

sentences.zh: 魏太昌初，起家前將軍、幹河軍主，除陽平郡丞。

translations.literal: At the opening of Former Wei's Taichang era he began his career as vanguard general and Yellow River garrison commander and was appointed Deputy Administrator of Yangping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Former Wei's Taichang era he entered service as vanguard general and Yellow River garrison commander and was made deputy administrator of Yangping commandery.

sentences.zh: 太祖曾使幷州，與果相遇。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor once went out to Bing Province and met Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai once went to Bing Province and met Guo.

sentences.zh: 果知非常人，密托附焉。

translations.literal: Guo knew he was no ordinary man and secretly attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo saw that he was no ordinary man and secretly pledged himself to him.

sentences.zh: 永安末，盜賊蜂起。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongan, bandits rose everywhere like bees.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongan era bandits swarmed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 果從軍征討，乘黃驄馬，衣青袍，每先登陷陣，時人號為「黃驄年少」。

translations.literal: Guo joined the army in punitive campaigns; riding a yellow courser and wearing a blue robe, he always led the charge in breaking formations; men of the time called him the "Yellow Courser Youth."
translations.idiomatic: Guo joined the army against them; mounted on a yellow courser and dressed in a blue robe, he always led the charge; men of the day called him the "Yellow Courser Youth."

sentences.zh: 永熙中，授河北郡守。

translations.literal: During Yongxi he was appointed Administrator of Hebei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era he was made administrator of Hebei commandery.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武敗於沙苑，果乃率其宗黨歸闕。

translations.literal: When Qi's Divine Sovereign was defeated at Shayuan, Guo thereupon led his clansmen and followers to submit at court.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi's Divine Sovereign was defeated at Shayuan, Guo led his clansmen and followers to submit at court.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，賜田宅、奴婢、牛馬、衣服、什物等。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor commended this and bestowed fields and houses, male and female servants, cattle and horses, clothing, and various goods.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai commended this and gave him fields, houses, servants, cattle, horses, clothing, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 從戰河橋，解玉壁圍，竝摧鋒奮擊，所向披靡。

translations.literal: Following in battle at He Bridge and lifting the siege of Yubi, in both he smashed the vanguard and struck fiercely; wherever he turned, the enemy was swept away.
translations.idiomatic: At He Bridge and in lifting the siege of Yubi he smashed enemy vanguards and struck fiercely; wherever he turned, the enemy broke.

sentences.zh: 大統九年，又從戰邙山，於太祖前挺身陷陣，生擒東魏都督賀婁烏蘭。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Datong he again followed in battle at Mount Mang; before the Grand Progenitor he charged forward into the formation and captured Eastern Wei area commander Helou Wulan alive.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 9 he fought again at Mount Mang; before Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai he charged into the enemy line and took Eastern Wei area commander Helou Wulan alive.

sentences.zh: 勇冠當時，人莫不嘆服。

translations.literal: His courage was foremost in the age; none did not sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: His courage was unmatched in the age, and all who saw it marveled.

sentences.zh: 以此太祖愈親待之，補帳內都督，遷平東將軍。

translations.literal: For this the Grand Progenitor treated him with still greater intimacy, appointed him area commander of the inner headquarters, and promoted him to general who pacifies the east.
translations.idiomatic: For this Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai drew still closer to him, made him area commander of the inner headquarters, and promoted him to general who pacifies the east.

sentences.zh: 後從開府楊忠平隨郡、安陸，以功加大都督，除正平郡守。

translations.literal: Later he followed Opening-Office Yang Zhong in pacifying Suizhou and Anlu and, for merit, was given the added rank of grand area commander and appointed Administrator of Zhengping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Yang Zhong, opening-office equal in three departments, in pacifying Suizhou and Anlu and, for merit, was made grand area commander and administrator of Zhengping commandery.

sentences.zh: 正平，果本郡也。

translations.literal: Zhengping was Guo's home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That was Guo's native commandery.

sentences.zh: 以威猛為政，百姓畏之，盜賊亦為之屏息。

translations.literal: He governed by stern force; the common people feared him, and bandits also held their breath for him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with stern force; the people feared him, and even bandits fell silent.

sentences.zh: 遷使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍、司農卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to bearer of the staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal in three departments, attendant cavalier at leisure, and minister of the grand commissariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was given bearer of the staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal in three departments, attendant cavalier at leisure, and minister of the grand commissariat.

sentences.zh: 又從大將軍尉遲迥伐蜀。

translations.literal: He again followed Grand General Yuchi Jiong in campaigning against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Grand General Yuchi Jiong against Shu.

sentences.zh: 果率所部為前軍，開劍閣，破李慶保，降楊乾運，皆有功。

translations.literal: Guo led his command as vanguard, opened Jianmen Pass, defeated Li Qingbao, and accepted Yang Qianyun's surrender—all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Guo led his troops as vanguard, opened Jianmen Pass, defeated Li Qingbao, and accepted Yang Qianyun's surrender, all with distinction.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝三年，授龍州刺史，封冠軍縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Deposed Emperor of Wei he was appointed Inspector of Long Province and enfeoffed as Marquis of Champion county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 of Emperor Fei of Wei he was made inspector of Long Province and enfeoffed as marquis of Champion with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 俄而州民張道、李祏驅率百姓，圍逼州城。

translations.literal: Before long the provincial people Zhang Dao and Li Zhi drove and led the common people to surround and press the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: Before long provincial men Zhang Dao and Li Zhi drove the people to surround the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 時糧仗皆闕，兵士又寡，果設方略以拒之，賊便退走。

translations.literal: At the time grain and weapons were both lacking and the soldiers were few; Guo devised stratagems to resist them, and the rebels thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Grain and arms were scarce and his troops were few; Guo devised a defense, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是出兵追擊，累戰破之。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent troops in pursuit and repeatedly defeated them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent troops in pursuit and repeatedly defeated them.

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，州境清晏。

translations.literal: Within a month the province was peaceful and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the province was at peace.

sentences.zh: 轉陵州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Ling Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to inspector of Ling Province.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，除隆州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was appointed Inspector of Long Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Guo was made inspector of Long Province.

sentences.zh: 加使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為公，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He was given the added ranks of bearer of the staff, grand general of agile cavalry, and opening-office equal in three departments, advanced in enfeoffment to duke, with fief increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He received the added ranks of bearer of the staff, grand general of agile cavalry, and opening-office equal in three departments, was raised to duke, and gained one thousand more fief households.

sentences.zh: 武成末，轉眉州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Wucheng he was transferred to Inspector of Mei Province.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Wucheng era he was transferred to inspector of Mei Province.

sentences.zh: 保定五年，授復州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Baoding he was appointed Inspector of Fu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 5 he was made inspector of Fu Province.

sentences.zh: 果性嚴猛，能斷決，每抑挫豪右，申理屈滯，曆牧數州，號為稱職。

translations.literal: Guo by nature was stern and fierce and could decide cases; he always checked the powerful and noble and set right those wronged and delayed; through several provincial governorships he was called competent.
translations.idiomatic: Guo was stern and decisive by nature; he always checked the powerful, righted the wronged, and through several provincial posts was called competent.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，卒於位。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 2 he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加絳晉建三州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted his former office, plus Governor of the three provinces Jiang, Jin, and Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously confirmed in his former rank and made governor of Jiang, Jin, and Jian provinces.

sentences.zh: 諡曰質。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Zhi.

sentences.zh: 子孝仁嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoren succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoren inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 孝仁幼聰敏，涉獵經史，有譽於時。

translations.literal: Xiaoren from youth was bright and keen, ranged broadly through the classics and histories, and had a reputation in his time.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xiaoren was quick and clever; he read widely in the classics and histories and won a good name in his day.

sentences.zh: 起家舍人上士。

translations.literal: He began his career as senior gentleman of the palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as senior gentleman attendant in the palace staff.

sentences.zh: 累遷大都督、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to grand area commander and equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to grand area commander and equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 出為長寧鎮將。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as garrison commander of Changning.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as garrison commander of Changning.

sentences.zh: 扞禦齊人，甚有威邊之略。

translations.literal: He resisted and repelled the Qi and had great ability to awe the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Qi at bay and showed great skill in frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 建德末，遷建州刺史，轉譙州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiande he was transferred to Governor of Jian Province, then transferred to Governor of Qiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Jiande era he became governor of Jian Province, then governor of Qiao Province.

sentences.zh: 大象末，又遷亳州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang he was again transferred to Governor of Bo Province.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daxiang era he was transferred again, to governor of Bo Province.

sentences.zh: 鄭偉等之以梁州歸款，時劉志亦以廣州來附。

translations.literal: When Zheng Wei and the others submitted Liang Province, Liu Zhi at that time also came over with Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Wei and his fellows submitted Liang Province, Liu Zhi at the same time came over with Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 志，弘農華陰人，本名思，漢太尉寬之十世孫也。

translations.literal: Zhi was a man of Huayin in Hongnong; his original name was Si, and he was tenth-generation descendant of Han Grand Commandant Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi came from Huayin in Hongnong commandery; his original name was Si, and he was a tenth-generation descendant of Liu Kuan, grand commandant of Han.

sentences.zh: 高祖隆，宋武帝平姚泓，以宗室首望，召拜馮翊郡守。

translations.literal: High ancestor Long: when Emperor Wu of Song pacified Yao Hong, as foremost man of the imperial clan he was summoned and appointed Administrator of Fengyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: High ancestor Long was summoned and made administrator of Fengyi commandery after Emperor Wu of Song conquered Yao Hong, on the strength of his standing as a leading member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 後屬赫連氏入寇，避地河洛，因家于汝潁。

translations.literal: Later, when the Helian clan invaded, he fled to the Yellow River and Luo region and settled his family in Ru and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Helian clan invaded, he fled to the Yellow River and Luo region and settled the family in the Ru and Ying area.

sentences.zh: 祖善，魏

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Shan, in Wei
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shan, in Wei,

translations.literal: (Da) [emended: Tian]
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Tian]

sentences.zh: 〔天〕安中，舉秀才，拜中書博士。

translations.literal: 〔Tian〕 An era, selected as xiucai, appointed Doctor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: during the Tian An era, passed the xiucai examination and was made doctor of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後至弘農郡守、北雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Later reached Administrator of Hongnong commandery and Governor of Northern Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to administrator of Hongnong commandery and governor of Northern Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 父瑰，汝南郡守，贈徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Father Gui was Administrator of Runan commandery; posthumously granted Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui served as administrator of Runan commandery and was posthumously made governor of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 志少好學，博涉羣書，植性方重，兼有武略。

translations.literal: Zhi from youth loved learning, ranged broadly through many books, was by nature upright and grave, and also had military stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Liu Zhi loved learning, read widely, and was upright and steady by nature; he also had military talent.

sentences.zh: 魏正光中，以明經徵拜國子助教，除行臺郎中。

translations.literal: In Wei Zhengguang era, summoned for mastery of the classics and appointed Assistant Instructor of the National University; appointed Lang in the Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's Zhengguang era he was summoned for classical learning, made assistant instructor at the National University, and appointed lang in the mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 永安初，加宣威將軍、給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongan, given the additional ranks General Who Proclaims Might and Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yongan era he was given the additional ranks of general who proclaims might and attendant within.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉東中郎府司馬、征虜將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year, transferred to Military Advisor of the Eastern Central Guard headquarters and General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to military advisor of the eastern central guard headquarters and general who conquers the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，除安北將軍、銀青光祿大夫、廣州別駕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, appointed General Who Pacifies the North, Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Vice-Prefect of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi year 2 he was made general who pacifies the north, silver-gleam grand master of splendid happiness, and vice-prefect of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 三年，齊神武舉兵入洛，魏孝武西遷。

translations.literal: In the third year, Gao Huan of Qi raised troops and entered Luoyang; Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Gao Huan of Qi marched on Luoyang, and Emperor Xiaowu of Wei fled west.

sentences.zh: 志據城不從東魏，潛遣間使，奉表長安。

translations.literal: Zhi held the city and would not follow Eastern Wei; he secretly sent covert envoys to present a memorial to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi held the city and refused to submit to Eastern Wei; he secretly sent covert envoys with a memorial to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武嘉之，授長史襄城郡守。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Wei commended this and appointed him Chief Administrator and Administrator of Xiangcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu praised this and made him chief administrator and administrator of Xiangcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 後齊神武遺兵攻圍，志力屈城陷，潛遯得免。

translations.literal: Later Gao Huan sent troops to attack and besiege; Zhi's strength failed and the city fell, but he secretly fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gao Huan sent troops to besiege the city; Liu Zhi's strength gave out and the city fell, but he slipped away in secret and escaped.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，太祖遣領軍將軍獨孤信復洛陽。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, the Grand Progenitor sent Army Inspector General Dugu Xin to recover Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 3 Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent army inspector general Dugu Xin to recover Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 志糾合義徒，舉廣州歸國。

translations.literal: Zhi gathered righteous followers and raised Guang Province to return to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi gathered loyal volunteers and brought Guang Province back to the Zhou cause.

sentences.zh: 拜大丞相府墨曹參軍，封華陰縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Appointed Staff Officer in the Ink Office of the Grand Chancellor's staff, enfeoffed as Baron of Huayin county with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made staff officer in the ink office of the grand chancellor's staff, enfeoffed as baron of Huayin county with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 加大都督、撫軍將軍，轉中外府屬，遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Given the additional ranks Grand Area Commander and General Who Pacifies the Army; transferred to staff officer of the Inner and Outer Staff; promoted to Director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the added ranks of grand area commander and general who pacifies the army, transferred to staff officer of the inner and outer staff, and promoted to director of the National University.

sentences.zh: 世宗出牧宜州，太祖以志為幕府司錄。

translations.literal: When Shizong went out to govern Yi Province, the Grand Progenitor made Zhi Records Officer of his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming went out to govern Yi Province, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai made Liu Zhi records officer on his staff.

sentences.zh: 世宗雅愛儒學，特欽重之，事無大小，咸委於志。

translations.literal: Shizong greatly loved Confucian learning and especially honored him; affairs great and small were all entrusted to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming loved Confucian learning and held him in special esteem; affairs great and small were all entrusted to Liu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 志亦忠恕謹慎，甚得匡贊之體。

translations.literal: Zhi too was loyal, forgiving, and careful, very much attaining the manner of aiding and supporting.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi too was loyal, forgiving, and careful, and showed the true manner of a good adviser.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，嘗謂之曰：「卿之所為，每會吾志。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor commended this and once said to him: "What you do always accords with my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai praised this and once told him, "What you do always matches my own intent.

sentences.zh: 」於是遂賜名志焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was granted the name Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he was given the name Zhi.

sentences.zh: 仍于宜州賜田宅，令徙居之。

translations.literal: He was moreover granted fields and a residence in Yi Province and ordered to move there.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted fields and a residence in Yi Province and ordered to move there.

sentences.zh: 世宗遷蒞岐州，又令志以本官翊從。

translations.literal: When Shizong moved to govern Qi Province, Zhi was again ordered to accompany in his original office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming moved on to govern Qi Province, Liu Zhi was again ordered to accompany him in his existing post.

sentences.zh: 及世宗卽位，除右金紫光祿大夫、車騎大將軍、儀同三司，進爵武鄉縣公，增邑通前一千戶，仍賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, appointed Right Golden-Badge Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies; advanced to Duke of Wuxiang county; fief increased to one thousand households including prior grants; furthermore granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Liu Zhi was made right golden-badge grand master of splendid happiness, general of chariots and cavalry, and equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies; he was raised to duke of Wuxiang county, his fief was increased to one thousand households in all, and he was granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 高祖時為魯公，詔又以志為其府司馬。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Duke of Lu, an edict also made Zhi Military Advisor of his household.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu was still Duke of Lu, an edict also made Liu Zhi military advisor of his household.

sentences.zh: 高祖嗣位，進授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，拜刑部中大夫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu succeeded to the throne, promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Opening-Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies; appointed Middle Grand Master of the Ministry of Punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu succeeded to the throne, Liu Zhi was promoted to grand general of agile cavalry and opening-office equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies, and made middle grand master of the Ministry of Punishment.

sentences.zh: 志執法平允，甚得時譽。

translations.literal: Zhi in enforcing the law was fair and even-handed, greatly earning the praise of his time.
translations.idiomatic: In enforcing the law Liu Zhi was fair and even-handed and won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 蓮芍界內，數有羣盜攻劫行旅，郡縣不能制。

translations.literal: Within the borders of Lianshao, bandits repeatedly attacked and robbed travelers; commanderies and counties could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Within the Lianshao region bandits repeatedly robbed travelers, and the local commanderies and counties could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 乃以志為延壽郡守以督之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhi was made Administrator of Yanshou commandery to supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi was therefore made administrator of Yanshou commandery to take charge of the problem.

sentences.zh: 志示以恩信，羣盜相率請罪。

translations.literal: Zhi showed them kindness and trust; the bandits one after another came to confess their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He treated them with kindness and good faith, and the bandits came forward one after another to surrender.

sentences.zh: 志表陳其狀，詔竝免之。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized explaining the situation; an edict pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi memorialized explaining the situation, and an edict pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 自是郡界肅清，寇盜屏息。

translations.literal: From then on the commandery borders were clear and calm; bandits and robbers ceased.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the commandery was quiet and banditry ceased.

sentences.zh: 遷使持節、成州諸軍事、成州刺史。

translations.literal: Transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs for Cheng Province, and Governor of Cheng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs for Cheng Province, and governor of Cheng Province.

sentences.zh: 政存寬恕，民吏愛之。

translations.literal: His government preserved leniency and forgiveness; people and officials loved him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was lenient and forgiving, and both people and officials loved him.

sentences.zh: 天和五年卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianhe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tianhe year 5.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、揚州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand General and Governor of Yang Province; posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand general and governor of Yang Province, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 子子明嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ziming succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziming inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 子明弘雅有父風。

translations.literal: Ziming was magnanimous and refined and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Ziming was cultured and dignified and had his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 歷官右侍上士、大都督、絳州別駕。

translations.literal: He successively held posts as Senior Gentleman Attendant at Court Right, Grand Area Commander, and Vice-Prefect of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as senior gentleman attendant at court right, grand area commander, and vice-prefect of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐極，除行臺郎中、順陽郡守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, appointed Lang of the Mobile Headquarters and Administrator of Shunyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Ziming was made lang of the mobile headquarters and administrator of Shunyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 子明弟子陵，司右中士、帥都督、涼州別駕。

translations.literal: Ziming's younger brother's son Ziling held posts as Middle Gentleman of the Right Office, Commandant Leader, and Vice-Prefect of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Ziming's nephew Ziling served as middle gentleman of the right office, commandant leader, and vice-prefect of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，拜姑臧郡守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang of Sui, appointed Administrator of Guzang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Kaihuang era under Sui he was made administrator of Guzang commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋加儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon given the additional rank Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was given the added rank of equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 歷衛州蔚州長史、幽州總管府〔司馬、朔州總管府〕長史。

translations.literal: He successively served as Chief Administrator of Wei and Yu Provinces, and at the You Province Governor-General's headquarters [Military Advisor, Shuo Province Governor-General's headquarters] Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as chief administrator of Wei and Yu provinces, as military advisor and chief administrator under the You Province governor-general, and as chief administrator under the Shuo Province governor-general.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔陽貨外叛，庶其竊邑，而《春秋》譏之；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In the past Yang Huo rebelled and went abroad, perhaps hoping to seize a domain, yet the Spring and Autumn Annals ridiculed him;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Long ago Yang Huo rebelled and fled abroad, perhaps hoping to seize a domain, yet the Spring and Autumn Annals condemned him;

sentences.zh: 韓信背項，陳平歸漢，而史遷美之。

translations.literal: Han Xin turned against Xiang Yu and Chen Ping returned to Han, yet Sima Qian praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin abandoned Xiang Yu and Chen Ping went over to Han, yet Sima Qian praised them.

sentences.zh: 蓋以運屬旣安，君道已著，則狥利忘德者，罪也；

translations.literal: This is because when fortune already belonged to stability and the way of the ruler was already clear, then those who pursued profit and forgot virtue were guilty;
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that when the times were already settled and the ruler's way was clear, those who chased profit and forgot virtue were guilty;

sentences.zh: 時逢擾攘，臣禮未備，則轉禍為福者，可也。

translations.literal: when the times met with turmoil and ministerial propriety was not yet complete, then those who turned calamity into fortune were acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: but when the age was in turmoil and ministerial duty was not yet fixed, those who turned disaster into advantage could be excused.

sentences.zh: 鄭偉、崔彥穆等之在山東，竝以不羈之才，邅回於鵞雀，終能翻然豹變，自致龜組，其知機之士歟。

translations.literal: Zheng Wei, Cui Yanmu, and the like in Shandong all possessed untrammeled talent, lingered at Goose Gate, yet in the end could suddenly transform like a leopard, attaining for themselves rank insignia of turtles and ribbons—is this not knowing the moment?
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Wei, Cui Yanmu, and men like them in Shandong all had bold, untrammeled talent; they lingered under the Goose Gate regime, yet in the end changed course like leopards and won high rank for themselves—were they not men who knew the moment?

sentences.zh: 王士良之仕于齊，班職上卿，出為牧伯，而臨危苟免，失忠與義，其背叛之徒歟。

translations.literal: Wang Shiliang serving in Qi, ranked among the upper ministers, sent out as a regional governor—yet at crisis he sought merely to save himself, losing loyalty and righteousness—is this not the sort who betrays?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiliang served Qi at the highest ministerial rank and was sent out as a regional governor, yet when danger came he sought only to save himself and lost both loyalty and righteousness—is he not rather one of the faithless?

sentences.zh: 令狐整器幹確然，雅望重於河右，處州里則勳著方隅，升朝廷則績宣中外。

translations.literal: Ling Huzheng had talent and capacity of clear solidity; refined renown weighed heavily west of the Yellow River; in the province and commandery his merit showed in the region; ascending the court his achievements were proclaimed within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Huzheng had unmistakable talent and force of character; his refined reputation weighed heavily west of the Yellow River; in the provinces his merit stood out in the region, and at court his achievements were known at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 而畏避權寵，克保終吉。

translations.literal: Yet he feared and avoided power and favor, and was able to preserve good fortune to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he feared power and favor, kept clear of them, and was able to end his days in safety.

sentences.zh: 不如是，亦何以立韙名、取高位乎。

translations.literal: If not thus, how could he have established a righteous name and obtained high rank?
translations.idiomatic: Had he not done so, how could he have won a righteous name and kept a high post?

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
